arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Heldman argued Section 1447(c) allows fee awards when cases remand to state court.
Mr. Heldman noted no statute grants fees to defendants who successfully defend removal.
Mr. Chilton stated Congress has granted defendants removal rights since 1789.
Mr. Chilton asserted the opposing sides removed the case properly without dispute.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether federal law allows a defendant to recover attorney fees. The defendant successfully defended a motion to remand the case to state court. the sides that brought the case argue the removal statute implies this fee right. the opposing sides argue no statute grants fees for this specific defense.

paragraphs: This dispute determines if defendants can recover costs for defending removal. It affects the financial risk of removing cases to federal court. It clarifies the scope of fee-shifting statutes in federal procedure.
